objective: Make game result cards and game detail pages read as one clear, league-neutral scoreboard story, including period scores, final context and a compact original Fanwire matchup illustration.
acceptance_criteria: Test-first: commit failing backend and frontend tests alone before implementation; the tests prove the preview contract and the visible card/detail states, and the implementation commit changes no tests.

Extend the existing game-final preview contract with nullable away and home period-score arrays sourced from the existing Game row; keep the existing read count and add no endpoint or database query. Regenerate backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts from the committed backend contract.

A game preview card shows both team names and final scores, date, verified game label/result and each available period score with Q1–Q4 and OT labels; overtime periods are numbered, totals reconcile to the existing final score, and missing line scores omit only the period row.

The game detail page presents the same teams, score, winner/result and date context as its heading hierarchy, followed by the existing period line score and both box scores; stat values and team names come only from the API response.

Add one original, code-native SVG matchup illustration using only court/ball geometry and the game’s existing team names, date and score; it contains no logos, crests, uniforms, team-color bars, player likenesses/photos, external asset requests or third-party artwork. Record its authorship as original project code in the PR.

At 320, 360 and 1280 CSS px, the page has no document-level horizontal overflow; box-score tables expose all columns through a labelled, keyboard-focusable horizontal scroll region with a visible scroll cue when needed.

The preview remains one link with an accessible name containing both teams and score; period values have visible text labels and a semantic table/list equivalent, and no result meaning depends on color or SVG alone.

Preserve the current light/dark token palette, focus treatment, minimum target sizes and reduced-motion behavior. If the preview-to-detail modal flow receives motion, limit it to a 150–200 ms relationship/state transition and disable it under prefers-reduced-motion; do not animate score values.

No new dependency. Keep the initial JS entry increase within 1 KiB raw and 512 bytes gzip; keep any new or enlarged async output within 8 KiB gzip total, and no built file at or above 500,000 raw bytes. Include the measured before/after bundle table in the PR.

Browser evidence in the PR covers a seeded game card and game detail at 360 and 1280 px in light and dark Chrome/Chromium, keyboard access to the table scroll region, missing period data, and a game with overtime if representative data is available; label fixture/override data synthetic.

Update wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x02-events.md and wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x08-frontend.md if their API/UI contracts changed, and update wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x06-feed.md when the public feed preview contract changes; the context-maintainer role can write all three module files.
